text:
Maya: quick question about the sample-app auth flow — we currently show exporting REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ORG in the README, but the node/python SDKs behave slightly differently when both env vars and a credentials file exist. Which precedence should the sample app demonstrate?

Chris: +1 this came up in onboarding. My vote: explicit env vars should win (for CI), then credentials file (~/.redwood/credentials) for local dev, then a shared cloud-config fallback. Keep it deterministic. :thumbsup:

Sam: agree. Also important: show how to rotate keys without downtime. Our current example has users editing env and restarting, which is noisy. We should recommend short-lived deploy keys + a refresh endpoint OR an atomic file swap for credentials file.

Eli: minor nuance: SDK parity — python/node/go should expose the same precedence and a programmatic override (config param) so apps can pin behavior. Otherwise samples diverge.

Maya: perfect. Drafted precedence order for the README snippet: 1) explicit per-process env (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ORG, REDWOOD_PROJECT) 2) per-user credentials file (~/.redwood/credentials) 3) system-level config (/etc/redwood) 4) metadata service (for infra, optional). Thoughts?

Chris: looks good. Add note that REDWOOD_PROJECT is optional and used to scope requests — if absent, the API key's default project is used. Also call out 401 vs 403: 401 = rotated/invalid key (should trigger refresh flow), 403 = insufficient scope/org mismatch (no refresh).

Sam: propose we add a tiny code example showing an automatic refresh attempt when receiving 401 and a single retry, with exponential backoff. Something like: 

```
// pseudocode
resp = client.request(...)
if resp.status == 401 and !retried:
  client.refreshCredentials() // reads ~/.redwood/credentials or calls login helper
  retried = true
  retry request with backoff
```

Eli: suggestion: SDKs should NOT automatically call the remote token-issuing API without an explicit opt-in (dangerous for server apps). They should attempt local refresh (file/env) and surface a clear error pointing to the recommended rotation flow. The CLI (redwood login) can do the remote flow.

Maya: good safety rule. For the sample-app README we should include both: (A) recommended pattern for long-lived server keys (rotate via CI and env injection), (B) recommended local dev flow (redwood login writes ~/.redwood/credentials and sample app picks it up).

devex-bot: FYI: added draft PR template for credential rotation examples -> https://git.redwood/samples/pull/42 (auto-note) :robot_face:

Chris: one more DX bug to capture — some users accidentally expose REDWOOD_API_KEY in docker images because our README suggests `ENV REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` in Dockerfile examples. We should change to `ARG` + runtime injection or show docker secrets example.

Sam: yes, update sample Dockerfile and add a warning block. Also include a tiny helper `redwood creds rotate --atomic` that writes new creds to ~/.redwood/credentials.tmp then mv + fsync to avoid race conditions. That will be part of the CLI follow-up.

Eli: can we make env var names slightly shorter for convenience? e.g., RW_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_API_KEY. I'm fine supporting both with env var mapping, but README should present the canonical one (REDWOOD_API_KEY) and mention RW_API_KEY as legacy alias.

Maya: canonical = REDWOOD_API_KEY, mention alias. I'll open a small doc PR with: precedence table, code snippet for 401 retry, docker guidance, and CLI rotate example. Will ping maintainers for parity checks across SDKs.

Chris: thanks — can you add a short test in samples that simulates a 401 then verifies SDK reads rotated creds from file on retry? Helps prevent regressions.

Maya: yes will add that. I'll also include a tiny checklist for SDK maintainers to ensure consistent env/credentials behavior across languages.

Sam: sounds great. :rocket:

Eli: :+1: once PR is up I'll run quick parity pass on go SDK.

Maya: PR opened: https://git.redwood/samples/pull/43 — tagging @Chris @Sam @Eli for review. Thanks all.
